newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosch net profit falls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bosch net profit falls in 1996.

text.p: German electrical engineering company Robert Bosch GmbH, stung by falling prices for car components, said on Thursday that group net profit fell 50 million marks to 500 million marks in 1996.

Speaking at the company's annual press conference, Bosch chairman Hermann Scholl said sales, however, would increase this year to 45 billion marks from 41.15 billion marks the year before. He also said Bosch was making strides toward expanding business outside Germany that should help profits.
Bosch, Germany's largest car components company, received too low a profit on its domestic sales and must concentrate on building business outside its home market, Scholl said.
"A further building up of our activities abroad, above all outside Europe, is necessary," he said.

The Chairman said he was sticking to his medium-term forecast of reaching a return on sales target of 10 percent, but addeded it may take longer to achieve that goal than by 2000 as had previously been thought.
The company reported a return on sales in 1996 of 4.1 percent, but Scholl said he expected a higher return this year.
Bosch attributed the lower profit to two factors. First, domestic customers were no longer prepared to pay a premium for car components or communications technology made in Germany.
That meant German manufacturers had had to cut their prices to keep up with cheaper foreign products.
In addition, Bosch had in recent years locked itself into long-term contracts with carmakers which included fixed annual price reductions in a bid to expand its market share.

Bosch had already reported a 15 percent increase in sales for 1996 to 41.2 billion marks. That figure, however, included acquisitions, without which sales would have grown a more modest five percent to 37.6 billion marks.
The company also confirmed previous statements about operating profit, saying the figure climbed 27 million marks to 1.67 billion marks.
